IdentityRegistry.note: Adds agent_address(uint64)address — a lean cross-contract getter. get_agent returns a struct with a dynamic string, which another contract would have to decode to reach the one field it needs.

ReputationRegistry.note: accept_feedback takes the settling transfer as a group transaction, reads the amount off it, AND resolves both ends through the IdentityRegistry — so a credit requires the payment to have gone FROM the client's registered address TO the server's. There is no pd_ ledger: replay is impossible because the payment is a transaction in the same group and consensus rejects a duplicate txid.

ValidationRegistry.note: submit_result and validation_response both resolve the caller against the IdentityRegistry by inner call. Only the assigned agent may submit; only the named validator may judge, or the client when no validator was named.

1.note: The live agent at api.ripar.io. new_agent takes the owner from Txn.sender, so this is the same account the agent's manifest names as payTo — which is what makes the A2A card's identity claim checkable rather than merely asserted.

2.note: The paying side, used as the attacker in deploy-v2.mjs's negative tests.

why: accept_feedback verified the payment was real but never checked WHERE it went, so one microUSDC moved between two addresses you control credited any agent id you named. Comparing server_agent_id != client_agent_id does not help: ids are not identities.

validation_response authorised with `client == sender OR validator_agent_id > 0`. The second clause is a fact about the JOB, not the caller, so the moment a validator was named the check passed for everyone — any address could mark any submitted job validated.

submit_result checked nothing at all, with a comment saying the client SDK would. A check that lives in the SDK is not a check: anyone could commit a result hash against anyone's job, which also locked the real assignee out by moving it to SUBMITTED.
Before 768559198 there was 768547170, whose scores counted two payment ids that resolve to no transaction at all — one of them 32 zero bytes.

verifiedBy.what: Deploys, bootstraps, registers two agents, then ATTACKS the result. Exits non-zero if any attack succeeds.
attacks: a payment to a third party cannot credit an agent — REJECTED
a payment from the wrong client is refused — REJECTED
a real client-to-server payment DOES credit — ALLOWED, jobs_paid 0 -> 1
only the assigned agent may submit a result — REJECTED for a stranger
a stranger cannot mark a job validated — REJECTED
the named validator CAN judge — ALLOWED, status 3 (VALIDATED)

knownGap: None of these contracts implements a DeleteApplication handler, so a deployment's 0.1 ALGO minimum balance can never be reclaimed. Four failed create attempts during this work permanently locked 0.4 ALGO in apps 768562625, 768562630, 768562697 and 768562713. Worth fixing before mainnet.
